text:
support-joe: FYI customer AcmeCorp reported a sudden p95 jump for text-generation in eu-west around 11:02 UTC. They see API requests taking 600-900ms (usual ~120ms). Sample trace ids: trace=cd9a1f, cd9a1g. They attached a curl timing and a span. Can SRE triage?

maria: ACK. Assigning. Which POP/region are they hitting?

support-joe: They say region eu-west (our eu-west POP). Sample request id: req_0a3f. They said it started ~2h ago after a config push to edge.

sanjay: pulling traces... I see a cluster of tls_handshake_ms spikes around that time and a lot of retransmits on egress to upstream CDN. p95 tls_handshake = 410ms (was 30ms). p99 = 750ms.

eli-network: I ran quick mtr from eu-west-pop-03 to customer origin via our edge egress:
```
Start: eu-west-pop-03 (10.2.3.4)
 1  10.2.3.1  0.8 ms
 2  203.0.113.21  1.2 ms
 3  198.51.100.9  420.6 ms  <-- big jump
 4  198.51.100.50  430.2 ms
```
Looks like one of our transit peers is introducing cross-AZ hairpin / queueing.

lia-prod: Customer also supplied curl --write-out timings:
```
name_lookup: 0.005
connect: 0.012
appconnect: 0.438
pretransfer: 0.439
starttransfer: 0.610
total: 0.612
```
appconnect ~438ms matches TLS handshake issues.

infra-bot: Alert: Edge-config deploy 1951234000 completed to eu-west-pop-02 at 10:55 UTC. No automated rollbacks.

maria: That deploy might have changed route-advertisement or health-checks. @eli-network can you check BGP adjacency/withdrawals for the time window?

eli-network: BGP logs show flaps between 10:53 and 11:03 for transit-peer AS64512 -> we briefly lost a more direct path -> traffic rerouted via remote PoP in us-east for ~8m. That explains hairpin and extra RTT + TLS time. I also see increased TLS retransmits on that link.

sanjay: Confirmed in traces: majority of latency is between edge->upstream CDN hop (TLS handshake duration). App layer latency is normal once TLS is done.

netbot: Route-change detected: prefix 198.51.100.0/24 withdrawn from AS64512 at 10:53:12, readvertised 11:01:36.

maria: OK immediate mitigations: 1) Roll traffic away from eu-west-pop-02 to eu-west-pop-01 and -03 via weight adjustment, 2) Temporarily lower DNS TTL for affected endpoint from 300->60 to allow faster client-side reprobes, 3) Open ticket with transit provider AS64512. Any objections?

lia-prod: For customer-facing action, I asked AcmeCorp to retry; gave them a short-lived region pin to eu-west-pop-01 and asked for new traces.

eli-network: Implemented weight change at 11:14 UTC, draining pop-02 (healthcheck override). BGP team has ticket 2026-487 with transit vendor.

sanjay: After weight change I see p95 drop back to ~140ms within 2m. TLS handshake p95 down to 45ms.

support-joe: Customer confirms latency improved after 11:16 UTC. They still saw a few delayed spans but overall fine. :thumbsup:

maria: Next steps: - Postmortem draft (owner: @eli-network) - Add automated detection alert for sudden tls_handshake_ms regression + correlated route-change events - Investigate why our deploy touched routing/bgp filters (owner: infra team).

eli-network: Taking postmortem. Preliminary cause: transit peer instability + edge deploy that changed BGP local preference ordering. We'll propose making BGP changes behind canary + automated rollback.

lia-prod: I'll follow up with AcmeCorp with an incident summary and credits.

maria: Nice triage team. Can someone add the traceroute + mtr outputs and a short timeline to the incident doc? Assign to me for review.

eli-network: Done, doc link: https://internal.redwood/inbox/incidents/1951234567 (will link full traces).

infra-bot: Reminder: schedule a postmortem meeting in #eng-postmortems.

maria: Added to calendar for tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Closing thread for live triage; reopen if customer sees regressions.

support-joe: Thanks everyone, leaving customer note and marking escalation resolved.
